kpis.label: European allies pledged at The Hague to reach 3.5% of GDP core defence spending by 2035; Germany's draft 2027 budget envisages ~€139.6B of total defence spending (€109.7B regular + €29.9B special fund, not yet final), so the demand runway is intact even as UK fiscal strain clouds BAE's interim 3% target

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD · DEFENSE TECH VC, PAST 2025'S $9.6B FULL-YEAR RECORD
kpis.label: Early-stage rounds are pricing at 17x-50x revenue; Anduril's ~$1.3B employee tender (Oct 13, $94.80/share, ~$90B valuation) closes Nov 9 with no outcome published yet, and the reported ~$100B primary round remains unconfirmed (Anduril told Reuters no decisions have been made). A Crunchbase News weekly roundup on Nov 6 listed Shield AI at the top of the week's US rounds with a '$2B raise plus $500M debt facility', but the underlying story could not be verified and may recap the March round at $12.7B

The stopgap (passed Sept 1) leaves the Pentagon on $838.5B versus a $1.5T FY27 ask and blocks new starts: Golden Dome has no base topline, and the $54.6B FY27 DAWG drone line cannot begin. After the Nov 3 midterms, drone and defense-tech stocks sold off on budget worries, and Jefferies expects the FY27 budget to land closer to the House's $1.15T than the administration's $1.5T request (which includes $53.6B for autonomous systems). The UK Autumn Budget (Oct 28) deferred the detail: plans to reach the 3.5% NATO target are to come in the upcoming spending review, with the path 'next year'

rows.angle: Oct 28 UK Autumn Budget: BAE and Babcock shares rallied through the budget (no figures confirmed), but the Chancellor said the plan to meet the 3.5% NATO target would come in the upcoming spending review and commentators said 'the precise path will come through next year'; no fresh share price confirmed (last ~1,832-1,899p in October, ~21% below the March ~2,360p peak); H1 sales £15.8B with a record £84.0B backlog and raised guidance (underlying profit growth 10-12%); ~22.5x forward P/E versus a ~14.8x ten-year average

private_watchlist.name: Anduril

The Sep 26 CCA production award (up to ~$5B split with General Atomics) is real production revenue.

private_watchlist.name: Saronic

private_watchlist.name: Helsing
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.8B round closed Jul 13, the largest defence-tech round in European history. Continues fielding the HX-2 strike drone in Ukraine.

bear_case.title: The stopgap budget freezes the programs the growth stories depend on
bear_case.description: The continuing resolution runs to Dec 11 and leaves the Pentagon on $838.5B versus a $1.5T FY27 request; it blocks new starts for 150+ programs, Golden Dome has no base topline and the $54.6B DAWG drone line cannot begin. After the Nov 3 midterms the drone group sold off on budget worries, and Jefferies expects the FY27 budget nearer the House's $1.15T than the $1.5T ask.
bear_case.counter: Congress has historically backfilled priority programs after a CR, and the reconciliation route could still deliver Golden Dome funding.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations remain stretched
bear_case.description: Palantir is a ~$430B company whose shares fell ~3.6% after a blowout print (revenue +96%) as the Nasdaq dropped ~4% over five days, so even beats are being sold; the S&P Aerospace & Defense sub-index sat near 32x forward earnings versus roughly 20x for the S&P 500 at last check — a premium the sector has to keep earning.
bear_case.counter: Palantir's 96% revenue growth, US commercial +148% and a Q4 guide ~$180M above consensus are far faster than higher-multiple software peers.

bear_case.title: Private-market valuations are drawing bubble comparisons of their own
bear_case.description: Early-stage rounds price at 17x-50x revenue, Anduril's ~$100B primary round remains unconfirmed (the ~$90B tender closes Nov 9), Shield AI is rumored at $20B+ after a March mark of $12.7B, and the Bank for International Settlements has compared the sector's pricing to the AI-infrastructure buildout it already calls bubble-like.

bear_case.title: The Pentagon's drone competitions keep favoring private newcomers over listed pure-plays
bear_case.description: Gauntlet II leaders Neros and Perennial Autonomy won real orders (Neros: ~$100M for 14,000+ FPV drones on Oct 1), while Red Cat's Teal Drones, Ondas's Ascent Aerosystems and Kratos all missed the top five.

bear_case.title: Contract wins and beats aren't rescuing the pure-play stocks
bear_case.description: AeroVironment beat Q2 estimates ($0.59 vs. $0.22 EPS) and won a $464.8M laser award yet fell to $102.55 on Nov 5 (-26% in a month); Ondas disclosed new counter-drone contracts on Nov 4 yet sat at $4.58 (-53% YTD); Red Cat touched $3.46. The Nov 6 rebounds (+9% to +15%) leave all three far below late-October levels.
bear_case.counter: Analyst consensus targets still sit well above current prices if backlog converts to earnings.

bear_case.title: Rheinmetall's guidance has now been cut twice in 2026 — execution, not backlog, sets the stock
bear_case.description: The Nov 5 Q3 print cut FY26 sales guidance to ~EUR13.2B and cash conversion to just over 0% (from >40%); 9M operating free cash flow is -EUR1.70B and net debt is EUR2.90B, and the shares fell as much as 16% intraday. Revenue and advance payments from the delayed Arminius order slip into 2027.
bear_case.counter: Operating margin beat (17.5% vs 14.8%), Air Defence guidance was raised, RBC and Jefferies kept Outperform/Buy, and the slippage is timing rather than lost orders.

bear_case.title: UK defence uplift is deferred, not delivered
bear_case.description: The Oct 28 Autumn Budget left the detail of the path to the 3.5% NATO target to the upcoming spending review ('the precise path will come through next year'), and some commentators expected more; BAE was roughly 21% below its March peak at last confirmed quote and trades at ~22.5x forward earnings. Hitting the target would cost roughly £10B a year extra amid gilt-yield pressure.
bear_case.counter: Roughly half of BAE's revenue is U.S.-linked and the order book is multi-year, so near-term revenue is less exposed than the share price implies.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: The record £84.0B backlog and raised guidance (profit growth 10-12%) are intact and BAE rallied through the Oct 28 Budget, but the 3.5%-of-GDP path was pushed to the spending review ('next year') and ~22.5x forward P/E is rich against a ~14.8x ten-year average — still the least-disputed name with ~half of revenue U.S.-linked. Directly accessible on UK platforms with no wrapper needed.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: The Oct 29 print (GAAP EPS +33% to $3.28, record $53.2B backlog at 3.2x book-to-bill, FY26 EPS guide raised to $12.25-12.35, $11B of THAAD/PAC-3 propulsion awards) is the strongest fundamental evidence in the group, while the Rheinmetall and Palantir prints this week show how much dispersion there is; post-earnings price unconfirmed (last ~$240.50, near the $232 low), so check entry. Also sits in the Space sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: AeroVironment

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: The Nov 5 Q3 print beat on operating margin (17.5%) but cut FY26 sales to ~€13.2B and cash conversion to just over 0% for the second time this year, with 9M operating FCF -€1.70B and net debt €2.90B; the up-to-16% share drop improves the price but the cash question stays unresolved, so wait for the Nov 27 capital markets day. Directly accessible from the UK without a wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Q3 revenue +96% to $2.3B with a Q4 guide ~$180M above consensus is the best fundamental print in the sector, yet shares still sold off ~3.6% after hours at a ~$430B market cap and ~80x+ forward earnings (last confirmed) — great business, price leaves little margin for error. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Nov 4 counter-drone contracts and a Nov 5 Stemme acquisition haven't lifted the stock, which sat at $4.58 (-53% YTD, -38% in a month) before a +15% bounce to ~$5.19, because much of the backlog is acquired or stock-funded — the evidence still doesn't support owning it here; Q3 (Nov 12 per earlier reporting) is the test. positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
